adapter_form.help.source: Internal key — same one used in items.source. Cannot be changed after creation.
adapter_form.help.category_reference: Curated type/subtype keys to use as the type/subtype values your fetch() returns — items.type/subtype are still plain text, so any other string works too, but a value from this list gets a category icon wherever items are shown.
adapter_form.option.type_api: API — calls an HTTP endpoint, maps the JSON response via config
adapter_form.option.type_custom: CUSTOM — a Python code snippet you write, executed on every poll
adapter_form.option.type_aiprompt: AI PROMPT — generates an item by calling an LLM on a schedule
adapter_form.field.use_ai_checkbox_label: Summarize this adapter's items with AI
adapter_form.help.use_ai: On by default. Turn off when this adapter's own field mapping already produces short, well-formed contents on its own (e.g. a nested {estacion.nombre} template) and the AI summarization step below is unnecessary. Independent of the global ACTIONS_AI_ENABLED switch — this only ever narrows it further for this one adapter, never widens it.
adapter_form.help.ai_prompt: Optional. str.format template used by the AI summarizer for this source only. Any of the item's mapped adapter attributes can be referenced as a placeholder — {source}, {item_id}, {extracted_title}, {extracted_contents}, {summary}, {url}, {event_key}, {type}, {subtype}, {policy}, {source_date_time}, {fetched_at}, {captured_at}, {rawdata}, plus the source's display name and site URL as {source_name} / {source_url} — an unknown placeholder just renders blank. Leave blank to use the current default (shown greyed above): the global ACTIONS_AI_PROMPT if set, otherwise the built-in prompt.
adapter_form.field.items_path_placeholde: blank = response root is the list, e.g. result.items
adapter_form.help.body: Raw request body, sent as-is (e.g. for POST/PUT).
adapter_form.help.preview_intro: Calls the endpoint with the connection settings above — no mapping needed yet — so you can see the real field names before configuring the mapping below, instead of guessing them blind.
adapter_form.sample.resolves_to_list: Items path resolves to a list of {count} item(s) — this is what "{test_fetch}" will iterate over.
adapter_form.sample.resolves_to_single_v: Items path resolves to a single value, not a list — pick one of the detected lists below, or leave it pointed at one of them.
adapter_form.sample.items_path_missing: Items path doesn't exist in this response. Pick one of the detected lists below.
adapter_form.sample.detected_lists_intro: Detected list(s) in this response — click to use one as the items path:
adapter_form.sample.showing_items: Showing {count} of {total_count} item(s) at the current items path. Drag a field name — from the list below or straight out of the JSON — onto a mapping row's value box, or click one to drop it into whichever value box you last clicked.
adapter_form.help.mapping_intro: How each item's contract field is built from one raw response item (see the sample above). The template box is a free-form construction — {Fecha} alone is a raw passthrough, plain text with no braces is a constant, and anything else — Sismo M{Magnitud} - {RefGeografica} — combines several raw fields into one string. A placeholder can also reach into nested JSON with dots, e.g. {estacion.nombre} or {datosEstaciones.estacion.medicion.valor} — if any step along the way is itself a list, its first element is used automatically. It can also use {uuid} for a stable, content-derived id when a source has no natural one, {source_name} / {source_url} for this source's display name and site URL, {date} / {datetime} for this fetch's start time, and {raw} / {response} for the current item / the entire fetched response, each as a JSON string. Drag a field name — from the list or the JSON below, at any depth — onto a box to insert it, or click one to drop it where you last clicked. Unlike every other kind of mapping problem, a dotted path that can't be resolved skips that item entirely (logged) rather than rendering blank.
adapter_form.sample.whole_item_chip_titl: Insert {raw} — the current item, re-serialized as JSON
adapter_form.sample.whole_response_chip_: Insert {response} — the entire fetched response (before items_path), as JSON
adapter_form.sample.datetime_chip_title: Insert {datetime} — this fetch's start date and time
adapter_form.table.mapping_date_format_h:
Date format
(only for a bare {field})
adapter_form.field.mapping_template_plac: e.g. {Fecha}, a constant, Sismo M{Magnitud} - {RefGeografica}, or a nested {estacion.nombre}
adapter_form.help.date_field: Normally a field name from the sample above. Can also be set to date or datetime to stamp every item with this fetch's own start time — useful when the source has no per-item timestamp of its own.
adapter_form.field.source_timezone_place: IANA name, e.g. America/Santiago — only needed if the date field is naive
adapter_form.help.python_code: Must define def fetch(config: dict) -> list[dict], returning dicts with an id key (title, contents, url, event_key, type, subtype, policy, source_date_time, raw are optional). Executed as trusted admin code — no sandboxing.
adapter_form.help.aiprompt_intro: This adapter asks the LLM provider configured under Actions — AI (the same ACTIONS_AI_PROVIDER / model / API-key settings the summarizer uses — no per-adapter overrides) to produce one fresh item at each occurrence of the cron schedule below, for content that must be re-generated every cycle, like a weather report. It calls the model at most once per cron occurrence per prompt (the item id is keyed to both), so set the adapter poll interval well below the cron period; between occurrences every poll is a cheap no-op. Editing the prompt below regenerates on the next poll rather than waiting for the next occurrence.
adapter_form.field.aip_prompt_placeholde: e.g. Write one surprising fact about amateur radio in two sentences.
adapter_form.help.aip_prompt_format: Required. str.format template — {date}, {datetime}, {source_name}, {source_url} are substituted; an unknown placeholder renders blank.
adapter_form.field.aip_title_template_pl: optional, e.g. Fact of the day — {date}
adapter_form.field.aip_event_key_templat: optional str.format template — blank = the item id
adapter_form.help.aip_test_fetch_note: "{test_fetch}" below does make one real LLM call (and does not store the result), the same way an API adapter's test fetch hits the real endpoint.
adapter_form.test_result.fetched_summary: Fetched {total} item(s) — showing up to 5, every mapped contract field.
adapter_form.field.policy_help: One Policy defines how often this source is fetched, and how its items are transmitted. Manage them under Config → Policies.
adapter_form.help.aip_cron_policy: This adapter regenerates on its Policy's fetch schedule — the Policy must use a cron fetch kind.
adapter_form.field.ai_on_failure_abort: Abort — don't chunk or transmit this item
adapter_form.help.ai_on_failure: What to do when the AI summarizer produces no real summary — AI disabled globally (ACTIONS_AI_ENABLED not true), no valid provider configured, the provider call fails, or it returns nothing. Use the extracted contents (default): store extracted_contents verbatim and keep the pipeline going; a provider call that raises an error is left to propagate and the item stalls until re-armed. Use the item title: store the item's title instead (falling back to the extracted contents) — the right trade-off for a time-critical source where something beats nothing. Abort: store nothing, record an item.ai_aborted audit event, and stop — the item is never chunked or transmitted. Choose this for sources whose raw extracted contents are meaningless without AI.
adapter_form.help.voice_replacements: Optional. Expands abbreviations in the spoken bulletin only — e.g. “km” → “kilómetros”, “SENAPRED” → “Senapred”. Matching is whole-word and case-sensitive. The transmitted AX.25 text and the stored summary keep the original abbreviations. Leave empty to disable.
